cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: carrying what you made into what comes next
cells.place: in the middle of a road you can't see the end of
cells.ask: offer the next step into not-knowing before you can picture where it lands — beginner's mind, every moment fresh, is what comes back.
cells.core: You're standing on something that started as a maybe and became real, and you're still holding it. The full weight is there — everything you set out toward, now actual, now yours to carry. And here's the thing: you're not forcing the road ahead into view. You've got enough light for the next step and you're taking it. What you built is real, and you're still moving.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying what you made, and you're still walking.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: carrying what you made past the point of what it can hold
cells.place: ahead of a road whose next step you're trying to force into view
cells.ask: let one thing you're carrying stay unfinished for a day — radiance without ego, shining because you are light, not to prove it, is what comes back.
cells.core: You've been gripping what you made — not just holding it, gripping — as if letting go of the shape of it would undo it. Every step ahead is loaded with the weight of where it all has to land, and you're bracing against a picture that hasn't arrived. You're carrying it forward so hard you've stopped being able to see what's actually next.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the outcome ahead of the road it's on.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: not carrying what you made because carrying it stopped feeling possible
cells.place: behind a road whose next step you've stopped expecting to see
cells.ask: let one thing you made be recognized — by you or someone else — without having to conclude anything about it; knowing that keeps deepening is what comes back.
cells.core: Something got made. You can see it — it's back there, real, finished in whatever way things finish. And you won't pick it up. Somewhere the weight of all it turned into stopped feeling like yours to hold, so you stepped behind it instead of into it. The road ahead is still there. You're standing at a door you already walked through.
cells.sheetLine: You made something real and you've left it behind you.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: already carrying what you made while describing it as still becoming
cells.place: inside a road you keep saying hasn't started yet
cells.ask: call one thing you've already finished, finished — in a sentence, out loud, once; beginner's mind, every moment fresh, is what comes back.
cells.core: You're steering this — the shape of what got made is running through how you talk about it, what you commit to, what you quietly let pass. But you hold it as though it were still ahead, still forming, still open. The carrying is already happening. Naming it as yours hasn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying it already. You keep calling it still becoming.
